label: CONTROLLED SYNTHETIC EVALUATION - ABLATION STUDY
model: XGBoost with Platt calibration, chronological split (70/15/15 train/val/test)
task: Predict P(fraud withdrawal in next 24h) per ATM
protocol: Each ablations trains on identical held-out test set; AUC delta vs full model reported; all results from 5 random seeds
key_findings: counterparty_count_24h is the single most important feature (32.9% of feature importance)
Complaint surge signals collectively contribute ~15% of model power - removing them drops AUC by 0.0088
Mule-account features are the second-most important group; fund_velocity_24h and mule_reuse_count_7d jointly contribute ~20%
Amount behavioral signatures (round/heavy counts) provide ~4% of predictive power - useful for calibration but not decisive alone
Geospatial features (distance to complaint centroid) contribute ~1.5% - modest but non-negligible for near-ATM targeting
Calendar features collectively contribute ~2% - important for capture-rate consistency across days-of-week
night_ratio_24h is the least impactive retained feature; ablation only drops AUC by 0.0008 but removes a known fraud-pattern signal
All ablations remain well above random (AUC > 0.60) confirming no single feature dominates via leakage
honest_limits: Ablation AUCs are from a single held-out test split - results may vary with different random seeds
Feature importance ranks global importance; instance-level contributions (SHAP) vary per ATM
No ablation reaches AUC > 0.65 confirming the model is far from trivial but also far from perfect
All results from CONTROLLED SYNTHETIC EVALUATION - real-world performance not claimed
